title.narrative: SLU Environmental monitoring for improved biodiversity and livelihoods DR Congo
SLU Miljöövervakning för främjad biodiversitet och hållbar försörjning DR Kongo

description.narrative: Projektet "SLU Miljöövervakning för främjad biodiversitet och hållbar försörjning DR Kongo" syftar till att hjälpa DR Kongo att uppfylla sina Agenda 2030-ambitioner att stödja hållbara försörjningsaktiviteter som bevarar ekosystemens och den biologiska mångfaldens integritet och funktionalitet när klimatet förändras. Detta innebär att man först använder miljöövervakning och miljöbedömning (EMA) för att bygga upp den vetenskapliga databas som omfattar biologisk mångfald och ekosystemens integritet, men också den sociala och ekonomiska dynamik som är avgörande för att säkerställa fortsatt ekosystemfunktion när människors välfärd förbättras. Sedan används denna EMA-databas för att stödja nationella institutioner med deras politik och internationella åtaganden. För att förbättra utsikterna till goda resultat kommer tyngdpunkten i detta projekt att ligga på skyddade områden och deras omedelbara omgivning. Projektet är ett tvåårigt pilotprojekt som kan fungera som en uppstartsfas för ett längre program. Projektet har tre mål: Datainsamling: Skapa en socioekologisk faktabas om biologisk mångfald i ett skyddat område för användning i lokal förvaltning av sötvatten och marina resurser mot bakgrund av klimatförändringar och resursutnyttjande. Kapacitetsförstärkning: Öka den nationella EMA-kapaciteten genom lämpliga utbildningsprogram. Samordning: Utforska möjligheterna att dela EMA-bevis och använda dem för att tillgodose lokala, regionala och internationella behov av evidensbaserad styrning av akvatiska ekosystem. Sveriges lantbruksuniversitet (SLU) kommer främst att arbeta med Universite Catholique du Congo (UCC) men även samarbeta med andra aktörer som Institute Congolais de la Conservation de la Nature (ICCN), WWF och Centre de Surveillance de la Biodiversite (CSB). Pilotprojektet kommer att fokusera på övervakning av den akvatiska biologiska mångfalden i Parc Marin the Mangrove och använda övervakningen för att kunna förbättra förvaltningen av den biologiska mångfalden så att intäkterna för lokalbefolkningen kan öka. Det kommer också att stödja utvecklingen av ett masterprogram inom miljöövervakning vid UCC och även förbättra samordningen på nationell nivå för övervakning av biologisk mångfald.

The contribution "SLU Environmental monitoring for improved biodiversity and livelihoods DR Congo" aims at helping the DRC fulfill its Agenda 2030 ambitions to support sustainable livelihood activities that will preserve the integrity and functionality of ecosystems and biodiversity as the climate changes. This involves first using environmental monitoring and assessment (EMA) to build the scientific evidence base that encompasses biodiversity and ecosystem integrity, but also the social and economic dynamics that are crucial for ensuring continued ecosystem functionality as human welfare improves. Then governance needs to use that EMA evidence base to support national institutions with their policies and international commitments. To improve the prospects for success, the emphasis of this project will be on protected areas and their immediate environs. This project is a 2-year pilot that can act as a start-up phase for a longer program.
The contribution has three objectives:
Evidence: Create a socio-ecological evidence base on biodiversity in one protected area for use in local governance of freshwater and marine resources in the face of climate change and resource exploitation.
Capacities: Plan for establishing national EMA capacity with appropriate educational programs.
Coordination: Explore the possibilities for sharing EMA evidence and using it to meet local, regional and international needs for evidence- based governance of aquatic ecosystems.
The Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences (SLU) will work mainly with the Universite Catholique du Congo (UCC) but also include collaboration with other actors such as Institute Congolais de la Conservation de la Nature (ICCN), WWF and Centre de Surveillance de la Biodiversite (CSB). The pilot will focus on aquatic biodiversity monitoring in the Parc Marin the Mangrove and use monitoring to be able to improve biodiversity management so that revenues for local populations can increase. It will also support the development of a master program within environmental monitoring at UCC and also improve coordination on a national level for biodiversity monitoring.

title.narrative: Agreement SLU Environmental monitoring for improved biodiversity and livelihoods DR Congo
Decision on contribution 16210 SLU Environmental monitoring for improved biodiversity and livelihoods DR Congo

description.narrative:
This conclusion of performance is for the first year of the two-year pilot project. During this first year:
-SLU has developed a strong collaboration with UCC(Universite Catholique du Congo) both regarding biodiversity monitoring and administration. SLU has even added a goal 0 to the 3 objectives they name "administrative capacity". The SLU controller has visited Kinshasa on several occasions and been able to build a strong relationship and mutual understanding of procedures and reporting with the UCC team. This is very important for a long term functional and sucessful collaboration. Not only when it comes to implementing activities but also regarding reporting. It is not always a controller is so involved and in combination with the visits from the project manager SLU has manged to strengthen the UCC capacity.
-Decided on Mabali reserve in Equateur as the pilot site for the biodiversity monitoring pilot and set up a collaboration with the research station there.(A first visit from Sweden to the site was done shortly after the end of year 1 of the project). This site is very promising and even better then the original one in mind for the project. There are also several other programs funded by the Swedish embassy in the Equateur province which could open up for synergies.
-A foundation for a full time MSc Program in Environmental and Natural Resources Management has been made. Training of students in the present Master program is ongoing and dicussions regarding on how to improve the curriculum has started.
-SLU/UCC has made connections to the Congo Basin Science Initiative which opens up for further capacity building and synergies between the two initiatives. Swedish teachers can be used in both programs and the biodiversity monitoring in the pilot site can make good use of students in the Congo Basin Science Initiative funded program.
-A scoping exercise on gender equality has been initiated
-Laid a good ground for increased activities in year 2 of the project on all objectives.
The change of project site that had to be done has caused delays in the implementation of the project. This is not due to SLU or UCC who have done what could be expected from them but is rather an effect of a malfuntioning ICCN(Institute Congolaise de la Conservation de la Nature). Finally SLU/UCC decided in dialogue with the embassy to change project site to Mabali. Since then things have progressed fast. This delay also made it impossible to engage students in the master program in field work the first year and the challenge to collaborate with ICCN also made the coordination work regarding biodiversity monitoring slower. However SLU/UCC adapted to the situation and has now set up a good collaboration with Mabali and 4 professors from Sweden visited there just after the end of year 1. The coordination on biodiversity monitoring will be focused on actors in Equateur to showcase a way of working and a national working group is underway. The focus is now to increase the speed of activities during year 2.
SLU has during the first year showed that they have the capacity to achieve the objectives and successfully run the program. It shows that they have long experience in this type of international collaborations and capacity strengthening. They have done good reporting and always had a good communication with the embassy including sharing possible external communication materials. The project was also mentioned in an article in Science. The team on the congolese side that has been put together is of really high quality, impressive. SLU has shown flexibility to adapt to challenges and take advantage of opportunities. They have done successful work on strengthening administrative capacity. During the first year of the project the embassy has met SLU representatives in Kinshasa on several occasions and also visited UCC. Both SLU and UCC staff are very knowledgeable and professional. It is very positive to see an academic collaboration between DRC and Sweden that can make a practical difference for local communities. This has a high value and is appreciated by government representatives.
